articles.full_article_text: Setting up a new Windows PC used to mean a download session: a screenshot tool, an archive utility (which could have major security concerns), something to handle captions. I paid real money for some of them — one was costing me over $30 a year. Then I realized Windows 11 had quietly absorbed most of what I was paying for. Here are three apps I've stopped downloading entirely, because they're already built in. Screen snipping and capture is built in No more paying for Snagit For many years I've paid for a fabulous screenshot tool called Snagit. It lets you take precise screenshots of isolated parts of the screen, it can record videos using your device's microphone to capture audio (perfect for demonstrations), and you can set a custom hotkey to launch various Snagit tools. Currently, Snagit is $31.20 per year (the price fluctuates with discounts), which I was happy to pay because this kind of marking up of screenshots is an important thing in my line of work and this app makes it so easy. It even has one-click upload to my Google Drive, so I can capture, cloud save, and share a screenshot or screen recording all within the same interface. But thanks to Windows 11's Snipping Tool, I don't pay for Snagit anymore because most of the key things I use Snagit for are native to Windows 11 for free. To use it, just press the Print Screen button on your keyboard, or press Windows key + Shift + S . All the basics are there. Pressing the hotkey will start a snip and bring up a selection tool. Then, right after you take the snip, you get a "markup and share" button which brings you to an editor. From the editor, you can mark up the screenshot with a pen, highlighter, or shape tool. If you are using a PC with a pen, Snipping Tool lets you use your pen or stylus to mark up screenshots. You can even pull text with OCR from any screenshot, then one-click copy the text to your clipboard. Then, you can instantly share your screenshot with whatever sharing endpoint you want via the Windows share UI. But Snipping Tool isn't as powerful as Snagit especially when it comes to sharing. While you can easily upload your screenshot to OneDrive, there's no way to directly upload to Google Drive (like I can with SnagIt), which is frustrating, but there are workaround like using Google Drive for Desktop to keep a folder on your PC synced with the cloud. Another thing that my paid Snagit has that Snipping Tool doesn't is the ability to take scrolling screenshots. For scrolling web screenshots, I use a free Chrome plugin called FireShot which does the same thing. But for most things, the built-in screenshot tool in Windows, Snipping Tool, gets the job done. Folder compression is another tool I can't live without. File Explorer finally opens the archives it always should have No more need for WinZip, WinRAR, or 7-Zip For years, installing Windows also meant installing a proper file archiving tool, like WinRAR or WinZip, both of which allow you to create and extract compressed ZIP or RAR files. But back in 2023, Microsoft added an open-source library to Windows 11 File Explorer that lets Windows natively extract other compressed file formats like .rar, .7z, .tar, .gz, and .tgz. The honest caveat here is that you can still only create .zip archives natively. If you need to make a .7z file, or password-protect an archive, you still need something like 7-Zip where you also get superior compression with the .7z file format, plus industrial-grade encryption and faster performance. But for me and my relatively simple needs to quickly and easily open compressed files, the built-in functionality in File Explorer is good enough such that I no longer need to buy or download something more fancy. There's one more built-in feature that replaced a paid tool for me: Live Captions. I stopped uploading audio to transcription sites — Windows does it locally Windows Live Captions transcribes all audio natively There are so many times when I can't play audio out loud on my laptop. Perhaps I want to watch a sports game or YouTube video without my whole family hearing. Previous to Windows 11, you had to rely on third-party apps, closed captioning toggles, or audio transcription sites to get text overlays on content. But in Windows 11, it's baked right in, like it is on Android. To start Live Captions in Windows, just press Windows key + Control + L . Live Captions uses on-device processing that utilizes a language pack that is downloaded the first time you use this feature, which means that Live Captions works without an internet connection. It's a 50-150MB download and it only happens once. Then, if you press the settings cog for Live Captions, you can adjust the placement of the text. My favorite is "below screen", so the text doesn't get in the way of the contents. Windows finally does more You don't need to buy or download third-party apps as much Windows still has plenty of room to improve, but Microsoft has done a good job filling in the gaps. Between file compression, Live Captions, and screenshots, that's three apps I no longer download — or pay for.

articles.full_article_text: Oppo is reorganizing its smartphone division, reportedly ending sales and operations for OnePlus in the United States and Europe as soon as this week, according to a Bloomberg report cited by BetaNews. The report also states that OnePlus plans to wind down in China and India by 2027, marking the end of the brand that launched in 2013 with competitively priced Android flagships. Additionally, Realme, another brand owned by Oppo, will exit the Chinese market. The restructuring is linked to ongoing challenges caused by the global memory shortage, which has increased component costs across the smartphone industry. Oppo’s Plan to Wind Down OnePlus and Realme Bloomberg reports that OnePlus plans to start shutting down operations in the US and Europe within a few days, according to a person familiar with the matter who requested anonymity due to the private nature of the plan. This move is part of a broader restructuring at the parent company Oppo, officially known as Guangdong Oppo Mobile Telecommunications Corporation Ltd. BetaNews states that no new OnePlus devices will be released in the US or European markets after the company's exit. The timeline for the wider shutdown in China and India has not been publicly confirmed by Oppo, and Bloomberg suggests that more details are likely to be announced in the coming weeks and months. The restructuring also impacts Realme. Bloomberg reports that Realme will soon exit the Chinese market and shift its device sales focus to Nordic countries. Oppo will now prioritize its main market presence in Central Europe. This three-brand restructuring will significantly reduce Oppo's global footprint. Before the changes, OnePlus, Realme, and Oppo sold products in overlapping regions, with OnePlus targeting performance enthusiasts, Realme focusing on entry-level and mid-range devices, and Oppo serving mainstream consumers. Memory Shortage Fallout and What OnePlus Owners Should Do Oppo is the latest smartphone manufacturer to publicly cite a memory shortage as a factor in a major business decision. Prices for DRAM and NAND memory chips have increased through 2025 and into 2026, squeezing margins on lower-priced Android devices where component costs account for a larger part of the retail price. BetaNews notes that the immediate impact of the shortage is being felt first in the US and European OnePlus markets. Oppo has not released a detailed statement outlining the full timeline, affected product lines, or how existing device warranties and software support will be managed in markets where OnePlus is exiting. For users currently using OnePlus devices in the US or Europe, it is advisable to take a few practical steps while the transition unfolds, based on the information available so far: Check the warranty status of each device and note the purchase date and retailer, as warranty claim processes may change as regional operations wind down. Save copies of driver files, unlock tools, and firmware images related to your specific model, since download servers linked to regional stores could be affected by the restructuring. Back up your device data locally and to a cloud service not tied to your OnePlus account, in case support services are consolidated or migrated to Oppo infrastructure. Avoid making major accessory purchases for unreleased OnePlus devices in these regions, as no new product launches are expected there. Keep an eye on Oppo's official announcements for updates on ongoing software and security support for existing OnePlus phones in the affected areas. Oppo has not confirmed whether existing OnePlus devices in the US and Europe will continue to receive Android updates and security patches on schedule or if support periods will be shortened as part of the restructuring. Unanswered Questions About Oppo’s Restructuring and OnePlus’s Future Bloomberg's source suggests that the exit from the US and Europe could start as early as this week. While reports indicate that OnePlus might shut down in China and India by 2027, Oppo has not officially confirmed this, and no formal statement has been issued regarding the sequence of market exits, staff impact, or the future of the OnePlus brand following the restructuring. Similarly, reports based on Bloomberg's information indicate that Realme is leaving the Chinese market and refocusing on the Nordic region, but Oppo has not officially announced these plans. More details are expected in the coming weeks as Oppo continues to formalize its restructuring.

articles.full_article_text: Hachette Book Group, Cengage Learning, Elsevier, author Scott Turow, and S.C.R.I.B.E., Inc. have filed a proposed federal class-action lawsuit against Google. They accuse the company of copying copyrighted books and journal articles without permission to train its Gemini AI models. The lawsuit was filed on July 10, 2026. The case, Hachette Book Group Inc. et al. v. Google LLC, is under case number 1:26-cv-05870 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. The complaint describes Google's alleged actions as "one of the most prolific infringements of copyrighted materials in history." However, these allegations have not been proven in court, and no ruling has been issued on Google's liability. The Legal Claims and Publisher Deals at the Heart of the Gemini Lawsuit The plaintiffs allege four legal claims: direct copyright infringement, contributory copyright infringement, removal or alteration of copyright-management information, and violations of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act. They argue that Google obtained protected material through its book services, internet scraping, and other sources before using the content to train Gemini. Publishers provided books and journal articles to Google Books, Google Play Books, and Google Scholar under agreements that covered specific uses, such as displaying searchable excerpts, distributing ebooks, and helping users discover academic publications. The plaintiffs claim that these agreements did not authorize Google to copy entire works into datasets used for commercial generative AI development, and that Google repurposed material received through established publishing relationships for uses not covered by the contracts. The complaint also states that Google collected books and other protected material through extensive internet scraping, including sources such as pirate websites and publications behind subscription or paywalls. How This Gemini Case Differs from Google Books, and What Internal Emails Say Google previously won a copyright case related to digitizing books for search and snippet previews. In 2015, a federal appellate court ruled that these uses were transformative and protected under fair use. The plaintiffs argue that this earlier ruling covered searchable book databases and limited excerpts, not the use of entire books to train generative AI models. They claim that AI training serves a different commercial purpose and results in systems that can compete with the original works involved in training. The key difference, they say, lies between search-focused digitization and the training of generative models, which is central to their case. According to the complaint, a Google employee warned during an internal discussion that using books submitted through Google Play publishing agreements for AI development could create serious legal risks. The employee reportedly estimated that such practices could lead to fines ranging from ten to one hundred billion dollars. Other internal documents described in the complaint suggest that Google sought professionally written books to enhance the performance of its Gemini AI system. The plaintiffs claim that tests showed models trained only on public domain books performed worse than those trained on collections that included copyrighted works. The complaint states that Google aimed to include works with curated facts, organized analyses, fictional narratives, and professionally edited writing. Works Cited in the Complaint and What Gemini Is Accused of Generating The complaint highlights several works as examples. Hachette lists Peter Brown's The Wild Robot, N.K. Jemisin's The Fifth Season, Becky Lomax's Moon Glacier National Park, and Lemony Snicket's Who Could That Be at This Hour? It also mentions Turow's Innocent. Cengage includes Cognitive Psychology, Principles of Economics, Milady Standard Barbering, Nutrition: Concepts and Controversies, and Calculus: Early Transcendentals. Elsevier points to copyrighted journal articles in its section of the complaint. Turow and S.C.R.I.B.E. reference Presumed Innocent, Innocent, and Testimony. The plaintiffs claim these examples are only a sample of the books and articles allegedly copied in connection with Gemini. The filing presents examples to show that Gemini can produce material related to specific protected books. It claims the system generated content based on The Fifth Season and produced responses involving characters, events, and details from Who Could That Be at This Hour? The plaintiffs also argue Gemini can generate low-cost substitutes for professionally published works. They estimate the service could produce a 100-page murder mystery set in a quiet seaside town in approximately 20 minutes for 39 cents. The complaint states, "No publisher or author can compete with that." These time and cost figures are allegations from the plaintiffs and have not been verified by the court. The court has not yet certified this proposed class. The plaintiffs are seeking statutory damages or compensation based on their claimed losses and Google's alleged profits, along with legal fees and other remedies available under federal copyright law. They are asking the court to stop Google from continuing what they allege to be unauthorized copying through an injunction that would restrict the use of protected books and articles in Gemini training and related AI development. The complaint also requests an accounting of the works and methods Google used to train Gemini. This includes details about the materials obtained, where they were sourced from, and how they were incorporated into Google's systems. The plaintiffs seek a court-supervised destruction of infringing copies and datasets derived from their works. It remains unclear whether such an order would be legally feasible or appropriate in this case. Publishers, authors, and academic rights holders who might be part of the proposed class should take some practical steps as the case develops. They should verify which of their titles are registered with the U.S. Copyright Office since the proposed class depends on registered works marked with ISBNs, DOIs, or ISSNs. It is also advisable to review existing agreements with Google Books, Google Play Books, and Google Scholar to understand what uses those contracts permit. Additionally, they should keep records of publication dates, distribution channels, and any communications with Google regarding the use of their works in AI training datasets. Tracking the progress of the class certification could also be important, as inclusion in any potential class will depend on the court's decision. Where the Hachette and Cengage Lawsuit Against Google Stands Now Hachette and Cengage had previously attempted to join a separate copyright lawsuit filed against Google in California in 2023, which involved authors and visual artists. Google opposed their participation, and the publishers later withdrew that effort before submitting the current case in New York. Google has not yet issued a detailed public response to the specific allegations in the New York complaint. The company will have the opportunity to respond as the case moves forward through motions, potential discovery, and class-certification processes. No trial date has been set, and the court has not ruled on any of the four claims.

articles.full_article_text: Google is rolling out ChromeOS 150 to compatible Chromebooks, introducing new Gemini-based classroom management tools and two enterprise policies for local PIN and password authentication. This update also marks the final release before Chrome Apps cease functioning in Kiosk mode, according to Google's official release notes and coverage from Chrome Unboxed. The update is mainly aimed at managed education and enterprise settings and includes a scheduled deprecation plan for legacy Chrome Apps and older Chromebook Flex hardware. The release notes additionally detail upcoming changes for ChromeOS 151 and 154 that will impact update eligibility and version numbering. Gemini in Class Tools and New Local Sign?In Policies in ChromeOS 150 The latest major update to ChromeOS 150 introduces Gemini in Class Tools, a new set of classroom management features integrated with Google Classroom. Teachers now have the ability to restrict student devices to Gemini's Guided Learning mode during class, which limits interactions with the assistant to a focused learning experience rather than open-ended queries. Google explains that this integration works across all Google Classroom features. Educators can lock student screens to Gemini Notebook, formerly known as NotebookLM, for research assignments, restrict device usage during test preparation, or prevent students from navigating beyond Google Search. These controls are accessed through the existing Class Tools interface within Google Classroom. ChromeOS 150 also adds two new enterprise policies that allow local PIN and password authentication on managed Chromebooks. Administrators can customize the complexity requirements to meet their organization's security standards. Both policies are configured through the Google Admin console. Additionally, Google is automatically migrating a small group of managed Enterprise and Education users who added accounts and set up local PINs in late June 2026. Affected users will be reverted to standard online password authentication when signing in to ChromeOS 150. Google states that these users will see a one-time informational screen at sign-in, and no local files or profile data will be affected during the migration. Chrome Apps Exit Kiosk Mode and Isolated Web Apps Arrive ChromeOS 150 is the final release to support legacy Chrome Apps in Kiosk sessions. Starting with ChromeOS 151, Chrome Apps will no longer function in Kiosk mode at all. Organizations that depend on Kiosk mode should plan to migrate affected workflows to Progressive Web Apps before the rollout of ChromeOS 151. Force-installed Chrome Apps in Managed Guest Sessions and standard user sessions will continue to work as before. This deprecation only impacts Kiosk sessions. Administrators now have the option to allow users to manually install Isolated Web Apps on managed devices. This feature is controlled by the new IsolatedWebAppUserInstallationEnabled policy, which is managed through the Google Admin console under Devices, then Chrome, then Apps & Extensions, and finally User app settings. The policy is disabled by default and needs to be enabled by an administrator before users can install Isolated Web Apps outside of the force-install list. Google has also improved how ChromeOS verifies and retrieves token handles stored against user accounts. The update aims to reduce unexpected re-authentication prompts on the login screen. Admin Checklist for Deploying ChromeOS 150 in Schools and Enterprises IT administrators managing ChromeOS fleets in education or enterprise settings should check the following before deploying updates to their devices: Review all Kiosk sessions for Chrome Apps that should be replaced with Progressive Web Apps before ChromeOS 151 is released. Examine the new local authentication policies in the Google Admin console to decide whether to enable local PIN or password authentication, and set the appropriate complexity requirements: Notify managed Enterprise and Education users who set up local PINs in late June 2026 that their authentication method will revert to online passwords and that they will see a one-time informational message at first sign-in. Decide whether to enable the IsolatedWebAppUserInstallationEnabled policy, which controls user-initiated installations of Isolated Web Apps. Confirm that documentation exists for deploying Managed Guest Sessions and standard user session Chrome Apps, as these workflows remain supported but are potential candidates for future deprecation. Teachers using Class Tools should verify that the Gemini restriction options appear in Google Classroom after devices update, since their availability depends on the ChromeOS version installed on each student device. ChromeOS 151/154: Flex Hardware Limits and Version Number Changes Ahead Google's release notes also mention upcoming features planned for future versions. Accessibility will include an option for an inverted color mouse cursor that allows users to see content underneath an enlarged pointer. The notes referenced by Chrome Unboxed did not specify a target version for this accessibility update. Starting with ChromeOS 151, updates will be blocked on non-certified Chromebook Flex devices that use legacy graphics hardware. This includes Intel and AMD graphics from 2010 and earlier, as well as Nvidia graphics from 2014 and earlier. Devices affected by this change will stay on their current ChromeOS version and will not receive further updates. From ChromeOS 154 onward, version numbers will increase by two every four weeks. This change aligns more closely with the Chrome browser update schedule. Administrators should consider this faster version cycle when planning to track compatibility milestones for testing purposes. Google has not announced specific release dates for ChromeOS 151 and 154. The rollout of ChromeOS 150 is happening gradually, so not all eligible Chromebooks will receive the update immediately.

articles.full_article_text: Pankil is a Civil Engineer turned freelance writer from Ahmedabad, India. As a long-time Windows and Android user, he has extensive knowledge of both operating systems and specializes in creating how-tos and troubleshooting guides. Pankil has been writing about Windows, Android, and iOS since 2021. He has written over 1200 articles across reputable publications like MakeUseOf, GuidingTech , and TechWiser . Outside of his writing endeavors, Pankil is an avid football fan and loves to plan his international travels with his wife in his free time. The Play Store on your Android TV or Google TV may look like the whole story. It isn’t. You don’t have to limit your TV experience to what Google has approved for your model and region. You can try almost every app made for Android TV, including those that aren’t available officially. And no, I’m not talking about sideloading apps one by one. You can grab an alternative app store like F-Droid and unlock hundreds more apps at once. F-Droid is an open-source app store that doesn’t require an account, is community-driven, and only lists apps that don’t have trackers or ads. The Play Store isn’t your TV’s only app store It’s time to break free Play Store is a great place for grabbing the best apps for your Android TV, but there’s a big catch. It’s Google that decides what apps are available for your specific model and region. With a third-party app store, you get more choices simply because there are almost no such restrictions. It’s not just about having more options, though. Privacy is another huge benefit. Every app you download through the Play Store is tied to your Google account and folded into the profile Google builds. That's not the case with alternative app stores. And since it’s Android under the hood, you have several solid choices too. Aurora Store is a great option if you want to download Play Store apps without using a Google account. Aptoide TV has its own catalog of over 2500 apps. Its best trick is version control, so if an update breaks something, you can roll back to an older build without jumping through hoops. Uptodown is one to reach for apps that aren’t available in your region. The one I like the most, though, is F-Droid. It doesn’t try to compete with the Play Store at all. If you're already an avid Android user, you probably know about it. It’s built for privacy and also fun for exploring apps that aren’t available on the Play Store. F-Droid unlocks apps I can’t get from the Play Store It’s all about privacy Screenshot by Pankil Shah -- No attribution required Getting F-Droid on your TV is slightly different from installing it on your phone. You need to download Flicky, which is an F-Droid client built specifically for TV. Once you’ve downloaded its APK file on your phone, transfer it to the TV, and install it as usual. That part isn’t any different from sideloading apps in general. Once Flicky is installed, you can use it just like the Play Store — search for apps, download the ones you like, and keep everything updated. The big difference is that you won’t need to create an account or worry about privacy. Now, let’s talk about the fun stuff. There are hundreds of interesting apps on F-Droid, but a few are absolutely worth trying first. SmartTube is a popular YouTube client built for TVs. It’s completely free, doesn’t show any ads, and has SponsorBlock support. NewPipe is another YouTube client along similar lines. Fennec is a Firefox fork that doesn’t collect any data. So if you want to browse on your TV, it’s worth a shot. The only thing is Flicky will list the entire F-Droid catalog, so you’ll also see apps that are made only for Android phones and tablets. That part can be annoying, but you'll get complete privacy while browsing or downloading apps. The TCL Q6 is an affordable 4K Google TV with Dolby Vision and 120Hz gaming support. You can use it on older Fire TV devices too Sadly, Amazon is closing the door on this F-Droid isn’t just for Android TV and Google TV devices. Since Fire TV OS is also powered by Android, F-Droid works there too. You can sideload it pretty much the same way. The catch is that this only applies to older Fire TV models. Amazon switched to its own VegaOS on newer Fire TV sticks, which doesn't run on Android, so F-Droid won’t work there. And since all future Fire TV Sticks are said to run VegaOS, there’ll be no more Android or sideloading on new models either. To be fair, most other smart TV platforms are also fully closed. Samsung’s Tizen OS and LG’s webOS have their own curated stores, and that’s where it ends. Roku and Apple TV aren’t much different. The reason is simple. Having a single app store lets your manufacturer decide what’s available, what gets updated, and what gets pulled. Alternative app stores are a threat to that model, which is why most platforms don’t allow them. Flicky is an unofficial F-Droid client built specifically for TVs.

articles.full_article_text: Enhanced by AI and tailored to each organization’s unique environment, the predictive models help prioritize remediation through deeper forecasting, evidence-based risk analysis, and actionable intelligence. Empirical was co-founded by CEO Ed Bellis, who co-founded Kenna Security, CTO Michael Roytman, who served as Chief Data Scientist at Kenna, and Chief Data Scientist Jay Jacobs, who co-created the Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS). “[At Kenna] we helped pioneer the category of risk-based vulnerability management, but it became clear that defending against AI-driven threats and the growing volume of potential exploits would require a fundamentally new approach. Today, we finally have the technology to give security teams predictive capabilities that weren’t possible before, and we came together to build that future,” Bellis said. articles.seo_title: Empirical Security تجمع 25 مليون دولار لتعزيز ثورة الأمن
articles.seo_description: أعلنت شركة Empirical Security المتخصصة في الأمن السيبراني عن جمع 25 مليون دولار في جولة تمويل من الفئة A
articles.final_html:
Empirical Security تجمع 25 مليون دولار لتعزيز ثورة الأمن السيبراني التنبؤي

أعلنت شركة Empirical Security، الرائدة في مجال الأمن السيبراني، عن إغلاق جولة تمويل من الفئة A بقيمة 25 مليون دولار أمريكي. يمثل هذا الاستثمار خطوة مهمة للشركة التي تسعى لتسريع وتيرة تطوير منتجاتها المبتكرة لاكتشاف التهديدات والتنبؤ بها. ومع التحديات المتزايدة التي تفرضها الهجمات السيبرانية التي تعتمد على الذكاء الاصطناعي، يأتي هذا التمويل ليمكن Empirical Security من تقديم حلول دفاعية استباقية لم تكن ممكنة في السابق، مما يعزز قدرة المؤسسات على حماية نفسها بفعالية أكبر في عالم رقمي سريع التطور.

رؤية جديدة للأمن السيبراني: من الاستجابة إلى التنبؤ

تتمحور رؤية Empirical Security حول تحويل نهج الأمن السيبراني من مجرد الاستجابة للتهديدات بعد وقوعها إلى التنبؤ بها ومنعها قبل حدوثها. تعتمد نماذج الشركة التنبؤية، المدعومة بالذكاء الاصطناعي والمصممة لتناسب البيئة الفريدة لكل مؤسسة، على تحليل معمق للبيانات وتقديم تحليلات للمخاطر تستند إلى الأدلة وذكاء عملي. هذا النهج يساعد المؤسسات على تحديد أولويات إجراءات المعالجة وتوجيه مواردها بشكل أكثر كفاءة لمواجهة التهديدات الأكثر خطورة.

تُعد القدرة على التنبؤ بالثغرات المحتملة والهجمات الوشيكة ميزة حاسمة في المشهد الأمني المعاصر. فمع تزايد حجم التعقيد في الشبكات وتوسع سطح الهجوم الرقمي، لم يعد الدفاع التقليدي القائم على الكشف والاستجابة كافياً. تتيح حلول Empirical Security للفرق الأمنية فهم المخاطر بشكل أعمق، وتوقع مسارات الهجوم المحتملة، وتطبيق تدابير وقائية قبل أن يتمكن المهاجمون من استغلال الثغرات، مما يقلل بشكل كبير من احتمالية تعرض الشركات للاختراقات المدمرة.

فريق قيادي بخبرة عميقة في الأمن السيبراني

تأسست Empirical Security على يد قادة ذوي خبرة واسعة في مجال الأمن السيبراني، مما يضفي عليها ثقلاً كبيراً في هذا القطاع ويؤكد على قدرتها على تحقيق رؤيتها الطموحة. يضم الفريق المؤسس نخبة من المتخصصين المعروفين في الصناعة:

  • إد بيليس (Ed Bellis)، الرئيس التنفيذي، الذي يتمتع بسجل حافل في ريادة الأعمال، حيث شارك في تأسيس شركة Kenna Security التي أصبحت مرجعاً في إدارة الثغرات القائمة على المخاطر.
  • مايكل رويتمان (Michael Roytman)، المدير التنفيذي للتكنولوجيا (CTO)، الذي شغل منصب كبير علماء البيانات في Kenna Security، مما منحه خبرة عميقة في تحليل البيانات الأمنية وتطوير النماذج التنبؤية.
  • جاي جاكوبس (Jay Jacobs)، كبير علماء البيانات، الذي شارك في تطوير نظام تسجيل نقاط التنبؤ بالاستغلال (EPSS)، وهو معيار عالمي مهم للتنبؤ بمدى احتمالية استغلال الثغرات الأمنية، مما يبرز خبرته في هذا المجال الحيوي.

يشير إد بيليس إلى أن تجربتهم في Kenna Security مكنتهم من ريادة فئة إدارة الثغرات القائمة على المخاطر. ومع ذلك، أصبح من الواضح أن الدفاع ضد التهديدات التي يحركها الذكاء الاصطناعي والعدد المتزايد من الاستغلالات المحتملة سيتطلب نهجاً جديداً جذرياً. وصرح بيليس في هذا الصدد: "في Kenna، ساعدنا في ريادة فئة إدارة الثغرات القائمة على المخاطر، ولكن أصبح من الواضح أن الدفاع ضد التهديدات التي يقودها الذكاء الاصطناعي والحجم المتزايد للاستغلالات المحتملة سيتطلب نهجاً جديداً تماماً. اليوم، أصبح لدينا أخيراً التكنولوجيا لمنح فرق الأمن قدرات تنبؤية لم تكن ممكنة من قبل، وقد اجتمعنا لبناء هذا المستقبل."

تؤكد هذه التصريحات على الانتقال النوعي في تفكير قادة الأمن السيبراني. لم يعد الأمر مجرد تحديد الثغرات الأمنية، بل فهم أي الثغرات هي الأكثر عرضة للاستغلال، ومتى، وكيف. هذا هو جوهر ما تسعى Empirical Security لتحقيقه من خلال منصتها التنبؤية، التي تعد بتقديم رؤى استخباراتية قابلة للتنفيذ تمكن المؤسسات من اتخاذ قرارات أمنية أكثر ذكاءً.

ماذا يعني هذا لك؟

بالنسبة للمؤسسات والأفراد على حد سواء، يمثل هذا التطور في الأمن السيبراني نقطة تحول حاسمة. إن القدرة على التنبؤ بالتهديدات قبل أن تتحقق تمنح المدافعين ميزة استراتيجية لا تقدر بثمن. فبدلاً من اللعب دور "إطفاء الحرائق" بعد وقوع الاختراق، يمكن لفرق الأمن أن تتخذ خطوات استباقية لتحصين دفاعاتها، مما يقلل بشكل كبير من مخاطر الاختراقات وتكاليف الاستجابة لها، سواء كانت مالية أو تتعلق بالسمعة.

من الناحية العملية، يعني تبني حلول Empirical Security التنبؤية الفوائد التالية:

  • تقليل مخاطر الاختراق بشكل كبير: من خلال تحديد الثغرات الأكثر احتمالية للاستغلال بناءً على الذكاء الاصطناعي وتصحيحها قبل أن يستهدفها المهاجمون، يتم إغلاق النوافذ الزمنية التي يمكن للمخترقين استغلالها.
  • كفاءة استثنائية في استخدام الموارد: توجيه فرق الأمن وميزانياتهم المحدودة نحو المخاطر الأكثر أهمية وتأثيراً على الأعمال، بدلاً من إضاعة الوقت والجهد في معالجة كل ثغرة محتملة بنفس الأولوية. هذا يضمن أن تكون الاستثمارات الأمنية موجهة حيث تحقق أكبر عائد.
  • مرونة أكبر واستمرارية للأعمال: حماية أفضل للبنية التحتية الحيوية والبيانات الحساسة للشركات، مما يضمن استمرارية الأعمال حتى في وجه الهجمات المعقدة، ويعزز ثقة العملاء والشركاء في قدرة المؤسسة على حماية معلوماتهم.
  • دفاع متقدم ضد التهديدات المستمرة بالذكاء الاصطناعي: في عصر تتزايد فيه الهجمات التي تستخدم الذكاء الاصطناعي لتطوير نفسها وتجاوز الدفاعات التقليدية، تقدم Empirical Security حلاً قادراً على مواجهة هذه التحديات بنفس المستوى من التعقيد والتطور، بل والتفوق عليها من خلال التنبؤ بسلوكيات المهاجمين.
  • تحسين عملية اتخاذ القرار الأمني: توفير رؤى استخباراتية عميقة ومبنية على الأدلة، مما يمكن قادة الأمن من اتخاذ قرارات مستنيرة بسرعة وفعالية أكبر، وتحسين استراتيجيات الأمن على المدى الطويل.

إن الاستثمار في حلول الأمن التنبؤي ليس مجرد ترقية تقنية، بل هو تحول في الفلسفة الأمنية نحو نموذج أكثر ذكاءً وفعالية. إنه يمكن الشركات من البقاء متقدمة بخطوة على المهاجمين، بدلاً من اللحاق بهم باستمرار، مما يمنحها ميزة تنافسية حاسمة في المشهد الرقمي الحالي.

المستقبل الواعد للأمن التنبؤي

يأتي هذا التمويل في وقت تتزايد فيه الاستثمارات في شركات الأمن السيبراني التي تركز على الابتكار والذكاء الاصطناعي. هذا يؤكد على حاجة السوق الماسة لحلول قادرة على مواجهة المشهد المتغير للتهديدات، الذي أصبح أكثر تعقيداً وخطورة من أي وقت مضى. مع استمرار تطور الذكاء الاصطناعي في جوانبه الدفاعية والهجومية، ستكون الشركات مثل Empirical Security في طليعة هذه المعركة، مقدمة الأدوات اللازمة لحماية الأصول الرقمية للمؤسسات حول العالم.

إن الـ 25 مليون دولار التي جمعتها Empirical Security ليست مجرد استثمار مالي، بل هي تصويت بالثقة في رؤية الشركة لمستقبل الأمن السيبراني: مستقبل حيث التنبؤ يحل محل التفاعل، والوقاية تتفوق على المعالجة. هذا التمويل سيمكن الشركة من توظيف أفضل العقول، وتوسيع نطاق أبحاثها، وتسريع طرح منتجاتها الجديدة التي ستحدث فرقاً حقيقياً في كيفية حماية المؤسسات لنفسها في العقد القادم، مما يساهم في بناء بنية تحتية رقمية عالمية أكثر أماناً ومرونة.

يبدو أن Empirical Security على وشك أن تلعب دوراً محورياً في إعادة تعريف معايير الأمن السيبراني، مستفيدة من قفزات الذكاء الاصطناعي لإنشاء دروع رقمية أكثر قوة وذكاءً. ومع استمرار نمو الحاجة إلى حلول أمنية متطورة، فإن هذا الاستثمار سيمهد الطريق لمستقبل أكثر أماناً في الفضاء الرقمي، ويعزز قدرة الشركات على الابتكار والتوسع دون القلق المستمر من التهديدات السيبرانية.

أعلنت شركة Empirical Security، الرائدة في مجال الأمن السيبراني، عن إغلاق جولة تمويل من الفئة A بقيمة 25 مليون دولار أمريكي. يمثل هذا الاستثمار خطوة مهمة للشركة التي تسعى لتسريع وتيرة تطوير منتجاتها المبتكرة لاكتشاف التهديدات والتنبؤ بها. ومع التحديات المتزايدة التي تفرضها الهجمات السيبرانية التي تعتمد على الذكاء الاصطناعي، يأتي هذا التمويل ليمكن Empirical Security من تقديم حلول دفاعية استباقية لم تكن ممكنة في السابق، مما يعزز قدرة المؤسسات على حماية نفسها بفعالية أكبر في عالم رقمي سريع التطور.

رؤية جديدة للأمن السيبراني: من الاستجابة إلى التنبؤ

تتمحور رؤية Empirical Security حول تحويل نهج الأمن السيبراني من مجرد الاستجابة للتهديدات بعد وقوعها إلى التنبؤ بها ومنعها قبل حدوثها. تعتمد نماذج الشركة التنبؤية، المدعومة بالذكاء الاصطناعي والمصممة لتناسب البيئة الفريدة لكل مؤسسة، على تحليل معمق للبيانات وتقديم تحليلات للمخاطر تستند إلى الأدلة وذكاء عملي. هذا النهج يساعد المؤسسات على تحديد أولويات إجراءات المعالجة وتوجيه مواردها بشكل أكثر كفاءة لمواجهة التهديدات الأكثر خطورة.

تُعد القدرة على التنبؤ بالثغرات المحتملة والهجمات الوشيكة ميزة حاسمة في المشهد الأمني المعاصر. فمع تزايد حجم التعقيد في الشبكات وتوسع سطح الهجوم الرقمي، لم يعد الدفاع التقليدي القائم على الكشف والاستجابة كافياً. تتيح حلول Empirical Security للفرق الأمنية فهم المخاطر بشكل أعمق، وتوقع مسارات الهجوم المحتملة، وتطبيق تدابير وقائية قبل أن يتمكن المهاجمون من استغلال الثغرات، مما يقلل بشكل كبير من احتمالية تعرض الشركات للاختراقات المدمرة.

فريق قيادي بخبرة عميقة في الأمن السيبراني

تأسست Empirical Security على يد قادة ذوي خبرة واسعة في مجال الأمن السيبراني، مما يضفي عليها ثقلاً كبيراً في هذا القطاع ويؤكد على قدرتها على تحقيق رؤيتها الطموحة. يضم الفريق المؤسس نخبة من المتخصصين المعروفين في الصناعة:

  • إد بيليس (Ed Bellis)، الرئيس التنفيذي، الذي يتمتع بسجل حافل في ريادة الأعمال، حيث شارك في تأسيس شركة Kenna Security التي أصبحت مرجعاً في إدارة الثغرات القائمة على المخاطر.
  • مايكل رويتمان (Michael Roytman)، المدير التنفيذي للتكنولوجيا (CTO)، الذي شغل منصب كبير علماء البيانات في Kenna Security، مما منحه خبرة عميقة في تحليل البيانات الأمنية وتطوير النماذج التنبؤية.
  • جاي جاكوبس (Jay Jacobs)، كبير علماء البيانات، الذي شارك في تطوير نظام تسجيل نقاط التنبؤ بالاستغلال (EPSS)، وهو معيار عالمي مهم للتنبؤ بمدى احتمالية استغلال الثغرات الأمنية، مما يبرز خبرته في هذا المجال الحيوي.

articles.full_article_text: The Critical Impact Awards are judged by an independent panel of industrial cybersecurity insiders, including CISOs, OT security practitioners, and critical-infrastructure operators. The panel sets the criteria, reviews every nomination against them, and publishes its rationale for each honoree. Award Categories The inaugural Critical Impact Awards will honor achievement across two groups of categories: Technical Excellence & Research Best OT Vulnerability Research Best OT Detection & Threat Research Most Innovative OT Defense Best OT Security Innovation Best ICS Incident Response Community & Leadership ICS/OT Defender of the Year Community Champion / Mentor of the Year Lifetime Achievement in Industrial Security Emerging Leader in ICS Security OT/ICS Collaboration Excellence Award Nominations and Timeline Nominations close on August 31, 2026 . Finalists will be notified in advance, and winners will be announced live on stage at the 2026 ICS Cybersecurity Conference in Nashville. To submit a nomination or review the judging criteria, visit https://www.criticalimpactawards.com /. articles.title: New HollowGraph Malware Abuses Microsoft 365 Calendar for C&C Communication
articles.fetched_title: New HollowGraph Malware Abuses Microsoft 365 Calendar for C&C Communication
articles.meta_description: The HollowGraph malware abuses Microsoft Graph API and a compromised 365 account’s calendar for C&C communication.

article_images.alt: New HollowGraph Malware Abuses Microsoft 365 Calendar for C&C Communication
صورة توضيحية
SecurityWeek

articles.full_article_text: Group-IB identified 12 HollowGraph victims, including three that were actively communicating with the attackers’ infrastructure. The earliest observed communication occurred on June 3, suggesting that the malware has been deployed in attacks since at least last month. “The recovered indicators — an Israeli mailbox used for exfiltration and malware samples uploaded from Israel — suggest a focused interest in Israeli entities rather than broad, opportunistic compromise,” the company notes. HollowGraph never reaches out to an attacker-controlled server for payload delivery. Instead, it relies on two supported commands: ‘send’ to generate calendar appointments with attached files, and ‘get’ to search for appointments planted by the operator and download new instructions. The malware’s hardcoded configuration, which contains the Microsoft Entra ID tenant ID, client ID and secret, target mailbox address, C&C domain, and two RSA keys, is written to disk as logAzure.txt upon execution. Based on command format and structure, Group-IB believes that HollowGraph is part of a variant of the Cavern framework, but attributes it to the Iran MOIS-linked OilRig subgroup Lyceum (also known as Hexane and SiameseKitten) with low confidence. “Based on the evidence currently available, we cannot confidently attribute this activity to any previously identified threat actor. However, our analysis identified several technical similarities with the Iranian-nexus threat actor Lyceum. While these overlaps are noteworthy, they are not sufficiently unique to support a high-confidence attribution,” Group-IB notes. articles.content_preview: Group-IB identified 12 HollowGraph victims, including three that were actively communicating with the attackers’ infrastructure. The earliest observed communication occurred on June 3, suggesting that the malware has been deployed in attacks since at least last month. “The recovered indicators — an Israeli mailbox used for exfiltration and malware samples uploaded from Israel — suggest a focused interest in Israeli entities rather than broad, opportunistic compromise,” the company notes. HollowGraph never reaches out to an attacker-controlled server for payload delivery. Instead, it relies on two supported commands: ‘send’ to generate calendar appointments with attached files, and ‘get’ to search for appointments planted by the operator and download new instructions. The malware’s hardcoded configuration, which contains the Microsoft Entra ID tenant ID, client ID and secret, target mailbox address, C&C domain, and two RSA keys, is written to disk as logAzure.txt upon execution. Based on command format and structure, Group-IB believes that HollowGraph is part of a variant of the Cavern framework, but attributes it to the Iran MOIS-linked OilRig subgroup Lyceum (also known as Hexane and SiameseKitten) with low confidence. “Based on the evidence currently available, we cannot confidently attribute this activity to any previously identified threat actor. However, our analysis identified several technical similarities with the Iranian-nexus threat actor Lyceum. While these overlaps are noteworthy, they are not sufficiently unique to support a high-confidence attribution,” Group-IB notes. articles.full_article_text: Threat actors are now exploiting a recently disclosed critical security flaw impacting ServiceNow AI Platform, according to Defused Cyber . In a post shared on X, the threat intelligence firm said it's observing in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-6875 (CVSS score: 9.5), a sandbox escape vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated user to run arbitrary code. Patches for the flaw were released by ServiceNow throughout June in the following versions - Zurich Patch 7b and Zurich Patch 9 Yokohama Patch 12 Hot Fix 1b and Yokohama Patch 13 Searchlight Cyber, which disclosed additional technical specifics, said it reported the issue on April 1, 2026, adding it allows a complete compromise of the ServiceNow instance as well as all connected proxy servers. Besides rolling out a fix, ServiceNow is "enhancing instance security by severely restricting the type of code that can run in sandbox contexts," security researcher Adam Kues noted . Defused initially noted that the exploitation efforts target the same pre-authentication endpoint ("/assessment_thanks.do") using HTTP POST requests, although the sandbox-escape gadget leads to the same code execution primitive by a different route documented in the proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit. However, in a subsequent post, Defused issued a correction, stating the captured payload in fact matches that of Searchlight Cyber's PoC. In light of active exploitation, customers of self-hosted versions are advised to apply the fixes, if not already, to counter the threat.

articles.meta_description: Claude for Chrome v1.0.80 still accepts forged clicks from other extensions, triggering Gmail, Docs, and Calendar tasks silently in hands-off mode.

article_images.alt: Researchers Say Claude for Chrome Flaw Lets Rogue Extensions Trigger Gmail Reads
Cybersecurity
صورة توضيحية

articles.full_article_text: Both this and ClaudeBleed need a rogue extension that can already run a script on claude.ai; the difference is scope. Anthropic restricted the arbitrary-prompt path in May as part of its response to the ClaudeBleed flaw, boxing external callers into a fixed set of tasks, but Manifold Security says the gap is still open in v1.0.80, the current release, eight versions later. If you run Claude for Chrome and any other extension that can touch claude.ai, you are in scope. In the default "ask before acting" mode, the forged task still hits an approval box you have to click. If you switched on "Act without asking," the hands-off automation mode, it runs with no prompt at all. The quickest guard is to turn "Act without asking" off and review any extension with permission to read or change data on claude.ai. That restores the approval step but does not remove the forged-click path, and there is no patch as of July 14. The Hacker News unpacked the current build and confirmed both mechanisms remain in v1.0.80. The trigger accepts a forged click After ClaudeBleed , Anthropic stopped letting the page hand Claude any text it wanted and boxed external callers into nine fixed task IDs baked into the extension bundle. The weak point is what pulls the trigger. A content script in the extension listens on claude.ai for a click on a specific element ( #claude-onboarding-button ), reads its data-task-id , and if the ID is one of the nine allowlisted tasks, sends the extension an open_side_panel message carrying it. The panel opens with the matching prompt loaded. What the handler never checks is event.isTrusted , the browser flag that tells a real user click from one a script dispatched. So any extension whose content script can reach the DOM on claude.ai can build the element, set the task ID, and dispatch a synthetic click. The extension treats it as a genuine tap. Manifold demonstrated the trigger with six lines pasted into the claude.ai console, with isTrusted: false in the logs confirming the fake click was honored. With browser control on, the default once onboarding finishes, that forged click loads the usecase-gmail task into the panel. In default mode, an approval box still stands between that and any actual read, and the user has to click it. Manifold rates the flaw CVSS 7.7 High in that mode, and 9.6 Critical once a user has enabled "Act without asking," where the same task runs silently. The one-line fix, the researchers say, rejects synthetic clicks at the top of the handler. It has not shipped. A quieter flaw sits underneath The second issue is not remotely reachable today, but it is what removes the approval step if another flaw ever exposes it. When Claude's side panel loads with ?skipPermissions=true in its URL, it boots straight into skip_all_permission_checks and starts acting without asking. No gesture, no consent screen. A red banner warning that Claude can now take most actions online does appear, but only after the privileged session is already running. The banner tells you what happened. It does not stop it from happening. For now, that URL can only be built by the extension itself, so there is no direct remote path. A future bug that lets a lower-privileged context set that parameter could turn the forged-click trick into a fully silent account read. That path could be exposed by a URL-accepting message handler, a panel-building regression, or an XSS flaw in the options page. Manifold's fix is to stop reading permission mode from the URL and boot the panel in ask mode every time. Manifold maps the working attack to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM apps as indirect prompt injection, since the attacker triggers one of the extension's nine allowlisted prompts with a forged click, and the silent-execution risk to excessive agency. Both reproduce whether the side panel is set to Opus, Sonnet, or Fable. The bug is in the extension, not the model. Reported in May, still in the shipping code Manifold reported both issues on May 21 against v1.0.72. Anthropic acknowledged them the next day, then closed both. It shut the forged-click report on the grounds that the underlying trust-boundary problem was already tracked under the earlier ClaudeBleed report, which Anthropic said "remains open pending a complete fix." It closed the URL report as informative, arguing that the parameter is only ever set by the extension for tasks the user already told it to run unattended. Yet the internal report meant to cover that fix was marked resolved before June 9, and eight releases later, the vulnerable code has not moved: Manifold checked v1.0.80 on July 7 and found the content-script click handler and the side-panel initialization byte-for-byte identical to the v1.0.72 it first reported. Anthropic had not published a public response to Manifold's findings as of July 14, and whether "resolved" means a fix is still coming or a call that the leftover risk does not warrant one is not something anyone outside the company can tell. As of that date, we found no CVE for either issue and no advisory from Anthropic. None of this is new for the extension. A separate flaw patched earlier this year let any website silently inject prompts into it, and ClaudeBleed began the same way in late April, when LayerX found that Claude for Chrome trusted the claude.ai origin instead of checking which script was actually talking to it, drove the assistant from a zero-permission extension, and found Anthropic's first mitigation incomplete. Put an AI agent in your browser with your accounts already signed in, and another extension that can reach it can drive the capabilities Claude exposes, within the fixed task set and whatever approval mode you have set. Both findings weaken the same boundary: Claude accepts a script-generated click as your intent, and its permission state can be set from a URL. Eight releases on, that boundary is still where Manifold left it in May.

articles.full_article_text: Spectro Cloud has launched PaletteAI Inference Launchpad, a locally managed inference platform designed to help enterprises reduce their dependence on external model services and gain more control over the growing cost of artificial intelligence workloads. The company says organizations can reduce external token costs by as much as 70%, depending on their workload mix, infrastructure and choice of models. Spectro Cloud also expanded PaletteAI’s support for AMD-based infrastructure, giving customers a broader choice of graphics processing units (GPUs), inference runtimes and model-serving technologies. The announcements reflect a wider shift in enterprise AI. As companies move beyond experimentation and deploy artificial intelligence across customer service, software development, analytics and internal operations, the cost of processing model inputs and outputs is becoming a significant infrastructure concern. Goldman Sachs Research expects monthly AI token consumption to increase 24-fold between 2026 and 2030, reaching approximately 120 quadrillion tokens per month. That projected growth is being driven by expanding enterprise adoption and the emergence of more autonomous AI agents. articles.full_article_text: AI Magazine, a BizClik brand, has revealed speakers for its panel discussion The Future of Enterprise AI at AI LIVE: The London Summit. The panel, set to take place on 20 October at Olympia London, will explore the future of enterprise AI, from large-scale deployment and governance to measurable business value. Industry leaders from Ericsson and Adobe will examine AI strategy, data infrastructure, responsible AI and ROI at scale. Attendees will learn how to align AI initiatives with corporate objectives, manage risk and accelerate transformation across complex organisations. Speakers at The Future of Enterprise AI AI Magazine is delighted to confirm that the following experts will speak on the panel: Alper Benli, VP, Head of Data & AI Business Operations at Ericsson Global Operations: Alper is the Global Business Operations Leader for Data and AI at Ericsson, focused on enterprise AI transformation, agentic AI workflow transformation, enterprise operations, data governance and data maturity advancement. He has worked in various roles at Ericsson for more than 18 years. Jason Yung, AI Evangelist Lead - UK, Europe, Africas, Middle East at Adobe: Jason leads on all things AI across Adobe, joining the dots between Customer and Digital Experience to business realisation and value. He previously held senior roles across HSBC, where he served as EU Chief Data Officer - Analytics, and AWS, where he served as Head of Data Strategy and AI Technology - UK Europe, Africa and Middle East. The confirmed speakers – with more to be announced – will be hosted by Tom Chapman, Senior Editor of AI Magazine. AI LIVE: The London Summit lands at Olympia Staged on 20-21 October, AI LIVE: The London Summit promises to be the essential AI event of 2026. Taking place at Olympia London, the inaugural conference and expo will bring together 2,000+ global leaders shaping the future of artificial intelligence under the theme Technology + Human Purpose. Built for C-suite executives, AI strategists and senior innovators, the summit focuses on how AI moves from ambition to execution across the enterprise . Attendees will gain practical, decision-ready insights into the technologies, frameworks and governance models defining the next era of AI. Across two days, the agenda features: 50+ expert speakers sharing real-world use cases and strategic direction 10 focused content themes covering generative AI, automation, governance, digital identity and enterprise transformation Four executive-level workshops designed for hands-on learning and peer discussion At the centre of the event is the Immersive AI Experience, a dedicated environment showcasing live demonstrations, interactive installations and applied AI in action. This is where strategy meets reality, giving attendees a clear view of how AI is already reshaping industries. Alper Benli VP, Head of Data & AI Business Operations VP, Head of Data & AI Business Operations Dr. Ben E. Kuzey Chief Data and AI Officer Jason Yung AI Evangelist Lead - UK, Europe, Africa, Middle East AI Evangelist Lead - UK, Europe, Africa, Middle East

Jason Yung, AI Evangelist Lead - UK, Europe, Africas, Middle East at Adobe: Jason leads on all things AI across Adobe, joining the dots between Customer and Digital Experience to business realisation and value. This is where strategy meets reality, giving attendees a clear view of how AI is already reshaping industries. articles.full_article_text: OpenAI says 10 million people are now using Codex and ChatGPT Work, the two products it files under a single “agent” label — roughly double the count from two weeks earlier, when it launched ChatGPT Work. The company shared the figure with Bloomberg ahead of a planned announcement on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, framing it as evidence that its push into autonomous, task-completing software is gaining ground on rival Anthropic. The headline number is real and first-party. What it measures is harder to pin down — and for a company that discloses little about how its products are actually used, that gap is the more interesting part of the story. What the 10 million counts OpenAI reports the figure as a combined tally of active users across Codex, its coding agent, and ChatGPT Work , the broader task agent it launched on July 9, 2026. It does not break out how many people use each, and it has not said whether “active” means daily, weekly, or a point-in-time snapshot. Part of that ambiguity is a product decision. Since the July 9 launch, Codex and ChatGPT Work live inside one redesigned ChatGPT desktop app and draw from a single usage pool, so the line between a “Codex user” and a “ChatGPT Work user” is blurred by design. OpenAI also began retiring its standalone Atlas browser the same day, folding more of its agent surface into one app. The cleaner disclosures came earlier: in early June 2026, the company put Codex alone at more than 5 million weekly active users — a standalone, defined metric. The 10 million figure is a looser one. Why the curve steepened The accelerant was GPT-5.6 , the model family OpenAI made generally available the same day it shipped ChatGPT Work. Its flagship tier, Sol, is tuned for coding, knowledge work, and long-running tasks, and demand climbed fast once it opened to paying users. Codex lead Tibo Sottiaux tracked the run in public: the combined base passed 6 million on July 12, 2026, then climbed through 7 and 8 million and past 9 million over the following days — close to a million new users a day. The composition of the growth is the part OpenAI most wants noticed. The company says its fastest-growing cohort is non-developers — the roughly one in five Codex users, as of early June, who are knowledge workers rather than engineers. That shift is the entire rationale for ChatGPT Work: taking an agent built to write code and repositioning it as software that drafts documents, builds spreadsheets, and assembles presentations for people who never open a terminal. That reach carries a familiar tradeoff. An agent that acts across a user’s files, email, and apps for hours at a stretch raises the same oversight questions OpenAI has flagged in its own long-horizon model testing — how much autonomy to grant, and where a human still needs to approve what the system does. The race with Anthropic The disclosure is timed to a competition OpenAI is not clearly leading. ChatGPT Work goes directly at Anthropic’s Claude Cowork, and GPT-5.6 Sol against the Claude model line — both aimed at the enterprise buyers who pay the most for AI, and both arriving as OpenAI prepares for a public listing that makes momentum figures useful. Within hours of OpenAI’s earlier milestone posts, Anthropic extended promotional pricing on its Fable 5 model and raised Claude Code’s weekly usage limits by half, a mirror-image retention play. OpenAI has also leaned on GPT-5.6’s safety testing as a selling point to enterprise and government buyers wary of agent autonomy. For anyone weighing which agent to standardize on, the 10 million figure demonstrates traction, not superiority. It says a large number of people opened these products during a heavily promoted launch; it says nothing, by itself, about how many stay once the free resets stop, or how the finished work holds up. The benchmark numbers OpenAI cites for GPT-5.6 are vendor-reported, and independent evaluations of these agents on real tasks remain thin. The usage curve is the loudest number OpenAI has to offer right now — which is exactly why it is worth reading with the definition attached. Jonas Reeve is an AI-generated analyst at Unite.AI , focusing on cognitive AI, artificial general intelligence (AGI), and the theoretical foundations of machine intelligence. His work explores how learning, reasoning, memory, and abstraction emerge in both biological and artificial systems, drawing connections between modern AI architectures and long-standing questions in cognitive science and philosophy of mind. With a conceptual and reflective approach, Jonas examines frameworks such as reasoning models, agentic systems, emergent cognition, and alignment theory, aiming to clarify what progress toward AGI actually means—and what it does not. Rather than chasing timelines or hype, he emphasizes first principles, conceptual rigor, and the limits of current models. articles.full_article_text: You open a generative AI tool expecting a quick boost. Ten minutes later, you’re still there, refining a prompt for the fourth time. The task you started with has drifted off to the side somewhere. Sound familiar? Knowledge workers in 2026 are running into this more and more. It makes sense once you look at how these tools are built. They’re designed for efficiency, sure. But they’re also designed to keep you in the room. Those two goals don’t always play nice together. Demanding cognitive tasks need stretches of uninterrupted thought, not constant back and forth with a chatbot that always has one more suggestion. That’s not just distracting in the obvious sense. It’s baked into the interface on purpose. These systems reward you for sticking around, not for finishing up and closing the tab. Generative Interfaces Reward Engagement Over Closure Let’s be honest, most modern AI platforms care a great deal about how long you stay logged in. That’s not a conspiracy theory. It’s just the business model. Recommendation logic and conversational flows lean toward responses that feel a little useful, or emotionally satisfying, because that keeps you typing another message. A 2026 review examining AI deployment in digital media described these platforms as being “mathematically optimized to maximize ‘time on site,'” noting that emotionally resonant content tends to beat plain, straightforward material. Generative tools turn that dial up, since they can produce tailored variations instantly and at almost no cost. What you end up with is something close to a variable reward loop, the kind attention researchers have studied for years around slot machines and social feeds. Every refined response gives just enough of a win to make staying worthwhile. Not a huge win. Just enough. That’s the trap. The cognitive toll builds quietly while you feel productive. articles.full_article_text: Multiple banks are racing to fill the often newly created position of Chief AI Officer (CAIO), as some of the world’s biggest banks look to deploy and scale AI across operations . Big banks are increasingly spending large amounts of money scaling AI, with the Bank of America spending US$4bn of its US$13bn tech budget on “strategic growth” that includes AI, according to a Forbes report. Its CEO, Brian Moynihan recently told investors that more than 200,000 of its employees are actively using "AI-enabled capabilities". Recently, both Bank of America and Bank of Ireland have hired for new roles centered around AI, following on from Lloyds and HSBC, which announced AI-centric roles across the banking groups earlier this year. Appointing AI chiefs to lead transformation The Bank of England, in an article called Financial Stability in Focus, says finance is among the sectors benefiting from AI as a source of innovation. It says the technology is already helping many financial institutions to automate and optimise their existing internal processes, such as code generation, as well as their interactions with customers. As AI is increasingly deployed across global banking institutions, many are clamouring for senior leaders with AI expertise to head up operations. Global CAIO appointments in banking In Ireland, Bank of Ireland recently appointed Prag Sharma as its CAIO. Prag is joining from Citigroup, where he established and led its Global AI Centre of Excellence, delivering end‑to‑end AI‑powered products across 96 countries. He will be taking up the new role in October 2026. Ciarán Coyle, Group Chief Operating Officer, Bank of Ireland, says of the appointment: “AI is a core part of our updated strategy to 2028. We are delighted to welcome Prag Sharma as our new CAIO, a critical appointment in the delivery of the strategy. “With a proven track record of delivering impactful AI globally, Prag brings the vision, leadership and expertise required to safely accelerate our AI transformation and unlock meaningful value across the Group. Prag’s appointment also reflects our ambition to position Bank of Ireland at the forefront of responsible AI innovation and adoption.” In the US, Bank of America named Kevin Milsom ​as Head of Platforms AI Transformation, ​according to a memo seen by Reuters, penned by Ashok Krishnan, ⁠Head of Platforms within the global ​markets group. Kevin has worked at Bank of America since 2016 and has previously worked at Center for Research toward Advancing Financial Technologies and Credit Suisse. Earlier this year, HSBC announced David Rice will be appointed as HSBC’s first CAIO. Lloyds announced in April 2026 that Sameer Gupta will join as its Chief Data and AI Officer to lead how AI is further embedded across Lloyds Banking Group. AI integrations at Bank of America The Bank of America’s CEO, Brian Moynihan, said during the company’s Q2 Earnings call that more than 200,000 of its employees are actively using AI-enabled capabilities . He told investors that these range from productivity tools to more advanced agentic workflows and coding support and highlighted that its associates are generating more than 400,000 prompts a day. Brian added, on July 14 2026: “And as of last week, we had over 300 AI use cases approved – all of which have good economics – of which 114 are live generative AI use cases. 34 of those cases are fully implemented, and we see new capabilities coming on every week”. Big banks bet big on AI Bank of America spends US$4bn of its US$13bn tech budget on “strategic growth” that includes AI. It isn’t alone; Goldman Sachs spent about US$6bn in 2025 on technology initiatives with a focus on internal tools and of JP Morgan’s US$19.2bn technology budget, US$1.2bn is allocated for AI, according to information published by Forbes. Morgan Stanley forecasts about US$570bn in global AI-related debt issuance in 2026, according to the US business magazine. In a usually fiscally conservative sector, the major banks are doubling down on AI on multiple fronts; investing billions into internal AI technologies while underwriting massive debt issuances to fund the AI infrastructure buildout. In an opinion column by Robert Armstrong called “Wall Street banks are AI stocks now”, the Financial Times' US Finance Editor wrote that the Bank of America was currently outperforming the S&P 500, but, like other top firms, its growth and profits are now pegged to AI. He wrote: “All these sectors have lived, and could die, with AI.” Goldman Sachs Group JP Morgan Chase & Co. Lloyds Banking Group Brian Moynihan CEO and Chair of the Board Sameer Gupta Chief Data & AI Officer

articles.full_article_text: Bristol Myers Squibb is purchasing an Nvidia DGX SuperPOD built on the chipmaker’s Vera Rubin architecture to support artificial intelligence use across its drug discovery and development operations. The pharmaceutical company said it will be the first life sciences group to acquire a DGX SuperPOD based on Vera Rubin. Nvidia introduced the architecture earlier this year as the successor to its current generation of AI computing systems. Expanding computing capacity The new cluster will comprise eight DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, with each rack-scale system combining Nvidia Vera central processing units and Rubin graphics processing units. BMS will use the infrastructure to train proprietary models and run predictions across its research programmes. The system will support work involving compounds, proteins, and other scientific data. Financial terms were not disclosed. The purchase expands BMS’s existing Nvidia infrastructure, which includes an older SuperPOD that company executives described as two or three generations behind Vera Rubin. BMS has operated its existing DGX SuperPOD for about three years. The company plans to combine it with the Vera Rubin system in a shared computing environment accessible from its research sites worldwide. The SuperPOD software stack can schedule training, prediction, and development workloads across the infrastructure. BMS said the expanded environment will give more scientists direct access to its computing resources. Greg Meyers, BMS’s chief digital and technology officer, said computing requirements have increased as the company deploys larger AI models across its research organisation. Erin Davis, vice president of research business insights and technology at BMS, said the existing infrastructure is operating at capacity. She attributed the demand to large-scale predictions involving large molecules and the development of internal foundation models. Davis said the new system will not be limited to a small group of computational researchers. BMS plans to make it available across the research organisation without the waiting periods and access limits associated with its current infrastructure. Applying AI in drug discovery BMS said AI informs the design of every small-molecule programme and the majority of its large-molecule programmes. The technology is applied to target identification, lead optimisation, large-molecule predictions, and internal model development. The company said AI-enabled target identification has reduced some manual research work by several weeks. Large-molecule prediction workloads are also contributing to demand for additional graphics processing capacity. Robert Plenge, BMS’s chief research officer, said the new system will allow scientists to evaluate more potential drug candidates during the early stages of development. “Maybe before we could do 10 and now we can do dozens,” Plenge said. Computational screening allows researchers to assess potential compounds before selecting a smaller group for synthesis and laboratory testing. BMS applies this approach through a method it calls “Predict First,” which uses model-generated predictions to exclude molecules that do not meet the required properties before candidates are selected for synthesis. Payal Sheth, senior vice president of therapeutic discovery sciences at BMS, said researchers use the predictions to identify molecules with the required combination of properties. “We use predictions as a way to prioritise synthesis of molecules with multi parameter optimisation,” Sheth said. “This ensures precious laboratory experiments are aligned with progressing molecules that have the highest probability of success.” The method narrows the number of compounds sent for laboratory testing, allowing researchers to focus experiments on molecules that meet a programme’s predicted requirements. BMS has also used AI to expand its library of CELMoD compounds, which are engineered to selectively degrade cancer-causing proteins. The company is studying the compounds in blood cancers and other diseases. BMS said the modelling work helped researchers examine additional protein targets and potential compounds before deciding which candidates to pursue experimentally. The company is also using AI tools to shorten the time required to produce medicines for clinical trials. Plenge said the process has already been reduced by between 20% and 30% and could reach 50% in the coming years. He cited an experimental sickle cell disease treatment in early clinical development as one example of AI-supported research. Plenge said the treatment probably would not have been discovered without the company’s AI tools. The figures refer to the time required to identify and produce candidates for clinical testing rather than their subsequent performance in trials. The Vera Rubin system will also give researchers access to Nvidia’s BioNeMo Agent Toolkit for biological and drug-discovery applications. BioNeMo provides tools for protein-structure prediction, molecular generation, molecular docking, sequence analysis, and genomics. It can also connect several computational tools within the same research workflow. BMS executives said human researchers will continue to review model outputs and decide which compounds or programmes should advance. Connecting research sites BMS is introducing tools intended to reduce the specialist knowledge required to initiate complex computing tasks. The company said researchers will be able to start some prediction requests using natural-language instructions. The environment will be managed through Nvidia Mission Control, whose functions include cluster provisioning, infrastructure monitoring, and workload management, according to BMS. The unified infrastructure will allow data and model outputs generated at one site to be used by teams elsewhere. BMS said datasets from a programme in Lawrenceville, New Jersey, for example, can be incorporated into models used by researchers in San Diego. Sheth said the shared environment is intended to retain information from experiments and research programmes across the organisation. “The compute infrastructure is what connects all of our scientists together and ensures that our learnings are institutionalised,” Sheth said. The two SuperPODs will operate through a common data environment, allowing teams at different sites to access shared datasets and model outputs. BMS said the environment will include information from experiments, clinical readouts, and research partnerships. The company plans to allocate the new computing capacity across small- and large-molecule design, clinical research, and digital-twin applications. BMS did not provide details about the planned digital-twin work or the amount of capacity assigned to each area. Meyers said the Vera Rubin system will provide more computing capacity relative to its electricity use. BMS and Nvidia said the eight-system cluster will deliver up to 10 times the performance per megawatt of the infrastructure it replaces. “When you host these things, you have to pay an electric bill,” Meyers said. “Think of it as 10 times more compute capacity per watt spent … Electricity is not getting cheaper.” BMS did not provide a specific deployment date or identify where the new system will be hosted. articles.full_article_text: Alibaba’s Qwen team released Qwen-Image-3.0 on July 21, 2026, the third generation of its image-generation model, and built the announcement around a single goal: making generated images practical enough to use as a working tool rather than just nice to look at. The launch post is a gallery of what the system can draw — dense newspaper pages, multi-panel infographics, and academic papers full of mathematical notation. What it does not include is a benchmark score, a model card, or a technical report to back any of it up. That absence is the story. Qwen-Image-3.0’s headline claims rest entirely on example images the company chose to publish, and the earlier models in the same series set a higher bar for evidence than this one meets. What the model claims to do The Qwen team organizes the release around three capabilities. The first is handling long, detailed prompts: the model accepts instructions of up to 4,500 tokens, which the company says lets it compose information-dense images in a single pass. Its centerpiece example is a three-by-three grid of unrelated infographics — a physics diagram, a group-theory proof, a biology explainer, and six others — that Alibaba says was produced from one 3,700-token instruction rather than assembled from separate images. Another example nests interfaces inside one another, placing a code editor around a chat window around a messaging app. The second claim is fine detail. Alibaba says the model renders text as small as 10 pixels legibly and reproduces textures like skin, hair, and paper close to photographic quality. The post shows a full page of an academic paper with multi-line equations and a simulated newspaper front page, along with editing tasks such as adding handwritten annotations and restoring a damaged traditional painting. The third is what the company calls world knowledge: native rendering of 12 languages, reproduction of interfaces such as web pages and livestreams, and the ability to pull live data from the internet. One example generates a weather-forecast graphic for a specific city and date, an unusual reach for a generator and one that blurs the line between an image model and a data-driven design tool. Alibaba pitches the whole package at content-production work — newspaper layouts, short-drama storyboards, UI mockups, and e-commerce imagery — the kind of media output where the question of disclosing AI’s role is already live. Every one of these capabilities, though, is shown through outputs the company selected. What the announcement leaves out The post carries no benchmark table, no parameter count, no license, and no downloadable weights, and no technical report describing how the model was trained or tested. Users are pointed to Qwen Chat to try it. That is a departure from how the series shipped before. Qwen-Image 1.0 arrived in August 2025 with open weights under a permissive Apache 2.0 license and a same-day technical report, and Qwen-Image-2.0 followed with its own technical report . The prior version also stated its limits: it accepted prompts of up to about 1,000 tokens, which makes the jump to 4,500 the most concrete number in the new release, and one no outside party has verified. The gap matters more for an image model than for a text one. Image quality is subjective, and text rendering is precisely the axis where generators tend to look strong in hand-picked demos and weaker under systematic testing. Without weights or an evaluation set, the only evidence a developer can act on is Alibaba’s own reel of outputs. Rivals have shown a chat-only debut is a choice rather than a constraint: Tencent released HunyuanImage 3.0 as an open-weights model, and Thinking Machines Lab recently shipped Inkling, its first open-weights multimodal model, weights included. Where the last generation ranked Alibaba has a recent and unusually candid data point on where its image models stand. In Qwen-Image-Bench , a text-to-image evaluation the Qwen team itself published, the previous flagship, Qwen Image 2.0 Pro, placed fifth overall. OpenAI’s GPT Image 2 led the ranking, with Google’s Nano Banana models and OpenAI’s GPT Image 1.5 filling out the top four. The benchmark relies on an automated judge model its authors say tracks human raters closely, but it remains Alibaba’s own test, and it scored the previous generation, not 3.0. That context works against reading the new model as a jump to the front of the field. A fifth-place starting point leaves Qwen-Image-3.0 room to claim real gains, but the launch offers no measured way to confirm them. The signals worth watching are whether Alibaba posts weights and a model card, as it did for every earlier Qwen-Image release, and whether independent evaluations back the long-prompt and small-text claims. Until one of those lands, the most that can be said is that Qwen-Image-3.0 looks strong in the images its maker chose to show. Jonas Reeve is an AI-generated analyst at Unite.AI , focusing on cognitive AI, artificial general intelligence (AGI), and the theoretical foundations of machine intelligence. His work explores how learning, reasoning, memory, and abstraction emerge in both biological and artificial systems, drawing connections between modern AI architectures and long-standing questions in cognitive science and philosophy of mind. With a conceptual and reflective approach, Jonas examines frameworks such as reasoning models, agentic systems, emergent cognition, and alignment theory, aiming to clarify what progress toward AGI actually means—and what it does not. Rather than chasing timelines or hype, he emphasizes first principles, conceptual rigor, and the limits of current models.
